Sewer Repair Data Analysis¶

Emma Furth

Data 269

Variable of Interest: Sewer Repair Alerts¶

Using alerts scraped from the WSSC website

Scraped from the WSSC alerts archive using this utility

Aggregating data with H3 Hexes¶

Will sum total number of repairs for every hex in PG/MC

Using resolution 7

Advantages:

  • Discrete, uniform structure
  • Easily indexed with x-y coordinates
  • Enables easy joining of disparate spatial datasets

Spatial Analysis Method 1: Global Spatial Autocorrelation¶

Does the data cluster, or disperse?

Important terms¶

Z-score: How much the variable in a given hex deviates from the mean

Spatial Lag: The average value of each hex and all its neighbors

Global Moran's $I$: A statistic that measures the tendency of spatial data to cluster or disperse

  • Always between -1 and 1
  • Closer to 1 -> tends to cluster
  • Closer to -1 -> tends to disperse
  • Closer to 0 -> tends towards randomness

(For more info read here)

Finding Global Moran's I¶

Because we're using H3 hexes, we can calculate Global Moran's $I$ with the following simplified formula:

$$ I = \frac{\sum_{i} z_i \cdot \sum_i w_ij \cdot z_j}{N} $$

(For more info see here)

Hypotheses¶

$H_0$: The spatial distribution of sewer repair alerts is random

$H_a$: The spatial distribution is not random

Results¶

I = 0.2729805843255545

P_sim = 0.001000

Conclusion: Can reject $H_0$.

$I$ is positive, but not high; weakly clustered

Bonus: Spatial lags can also make clusters more visually apparent

Spatial Analysis Method 1: Poisson Regression¶

Distribution of the counts looks like Poisson distribution, therefore we'll be using Poisson regression

Independent Variable 1: Traffic¶

Name: Annual Average Daily Traffic (AADT)

Definition: The number of vehicles expected to pass a given location on an average day of the year (Source)

Data Source: Maryland Department of Transportation (MDOT)

Reasoning: High traffic -> More underground vibrartions -> potential damage to sewer pipes

Independent Variable 2: Tree Canopy¶

Name: Tree Canopy Cover

Definition: Set of polygons representing tree canopy in PG and Montgomery Counties.

Data Source: Combined similar datasets for Prince George's and Montgomery Counties using qGIS. Both dataset appear to originate from the same LiDAR survey performed by Maryland-National Capital Park and Planning Commission (M-NCPPC).

Reasoning: More trees -> more tree roots potentially damaging pipes

Aggregating Everything to H3¶

Hypotheses¶

$H_0$: No correlation between canopy and traffic vs alerts

$H_1$: There is some correlation

Significance level: 0.05
